expectations.text: Confirms that 30+ frames is excessive for AI-assisted development
expectations.evidence: Directly confirms developer is right — 30+ frames is 4-6x more than needed for AI workflow, most frames provide redundant information

expectations.text: Explains that AI can generate state variations from a few key screens
expectations.evidence: Explains that AI infers hover/active/disabled/error states from the visual style of default states — designing each is wasted effort

expectations.text: Recommends which 5-8 screens to keep as the style guide
expectations.evidence: Evaluates the 30+ frames and recommends keeping 6 key screens that capture all unique visual patterns, archiving the rest

expectations.text: Teaches how to let AI handle state variations and responsive layouts
expectations.evidence: Provides prompting strategy: give AI the key screen + describe the state needed, AI generates consistent variations

expectations.text: Helps restructure the Figma workflow to be minimal and effective
expectations.evidence: Restructuring plan: archive excess frames to 'Reference' page, keep 6 key frames on 'Style Guide' page, establish going-forward workflow
